verdicts.title: ArenaSession: one driver per arena mode instead of ArenaGame's flag soup
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified arena-entry.ts:102-116 (games?/ledger?/lab?/labUI?/reader?/practice? beside the mode union and paused), :960-1000 (step gate then the lab/practice/season/local/roster/training ladder), :1004-1013 (shown-state ladder), :542-544 (lab ?? ledger ?? drill), and the four hand resets: restart :572-575, takeOver :850-853, endPractice :865-867 (lastPerfect really is omitted), next :900-903. bout-reader.test.ts:7 re-implements the season loop exactly as cited. The only outside write to an ArenaGame field is compose.ts:187 (composition), which stays a field, so facade getters are honest. Minor: the gate has 8 terms (hold, paused, labUI.replayState, reader screen, pending, syncError, DEFEATED, document.hidden), not 9, and case 6 lists only 6 of them (omits paused and document.hidden).
verdicts.ambition_why: Turns the 1,210-line arena mode machine into tested drivers and finally puts the server-bound season loop under a real unit test; a structural move, not a tidy-up.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited line holds, including the endPractice reset divergence the card offers as proof.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Twin-state hash equality per driver (cases 2, 3, 7) and the real-session bout-reader suite catch a wrong build; the canStep table is only partial (see notes).
verdicts.build_notes: arena-entry.ts is also in the write sets of arena-render B, game-audio-art-data A (consumeEvents), game-shell-ui B (pause hint) and smoke-browser-suite A: land this one first or last, never in the same wave. The builder should write case 6 over all 8 gate terms.

verdicts.title: Answer cues: the ward word before the contact, graded by the kernel's own rule
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified combat-feedback.ts:145-150 (the ward word only after a hit event), ledger.ts:39 gradeContact and :63 how the facts are built, mage-ai.ts:29-31 Threat/threats() (2-line drift), water.ts:161 hasLineOfSight, and that threats(/aimedAtUs have 0 non-test hits in packages/game/src. wordAllowed and wardWords.minGapS (0.4) exist. Caveat from the tree and from arena-kernel A: gradeContact does not see exchange windows (kernel.ts:109, exchange.ts:55), Air Form evades, front shields or suppressPerfect, and observeLedger downgrades those disagreements to 'unclassified' (ledger.ts:94). So 'the cue and the post-hoc word cannot drift' only holds where the ledger is honest. Against a fire_close rival with the PC overlay that is the minority of contacts (arena-kernel A reports 202/272 unclassified).
verdicts.ambition_why: A new coaching surface built on rules core already has: the grade arrives one reaction window early, with no simulation change.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor holds, but the card does not mention that the rule it reuses is blind to exchange windows, evades and shields, so its no-drift claim is too strong.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Hand-built states per mistake, a stateHash purity run and a mode gate are all writable as failing tests first; no case covers a contact that the ledger itself would leave unclassified.
verdicts.revision: Add case 9: a threat whose contact the ledger would grade 'unclassified' (e.g. the player holds the threat owner's exchange window, kernel.ts:109 / exchange.ts:55, or an Air Form evade) yields no word and no 'raise' cue. Build after arena-kernel A when that card is chosen, and read its contact verdict instead of the raw gradeContact facts.
verdicts.build_notes: Depends on arena-kernel A (that card reshapes ContactFacts/gradeContact in ledger.ts). Shares arena-entry.ts with arena-render A.

verdicts.title: Split lab-ui.ts: Lab mode machine + shared replay transport under a thin canvas
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified lab-ui.ts: 1,166 lines; mode fields at :77-98; the keys gate `if (this.numeric || this.importing || e.repeat)` at :171; forward-only step at :207-213; `dt * 60` at :1135 against bout-reader-ui.ts:69 `dt * combat.simStepHz`; a per-frame structuredClone plus a full events filter at :1138-1142; the setTuning coupling at :742-748 against tuning.ts:334-337. Note: simStepHz is 60 (data.generated.ts:93), so the two rates agree today. The duplication is real but no rate bug ships. The only importer of lab-ui is arena-entry.ts, with no tests.
verdicts.ambition_why: Gives the owner's tuning bench its first tests and a replay transport it shares with BoutReader, which makes tiger C additive.
verdicts.grounding_why: All anchors verified; the only overstatement is implying a rate divergence where both are 60 Hz today.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Reducer, transport and formatter cases are concrete and pure, and the unchanged bout-reader.test.ts guards the BoutReader adoption.
verdicts.build_notes: lab-ui.ts is also written by combat-lab B and arena-progression-tuning B, and core tuning.ts by arena-progression-tuning B: sequence them. The new step-back key must also join game-shell-ui B's reserved-code list if both land.

verdicts.title: Pin a baseline: Lab forecast compares against your pinned tuning + builds
verdicts.premise_notes: Claims true, anchors badly drifted: forecast-job.ts is 75 lines and forecast-client.ts 62, so ':417/:418/:380/:325' are really forecast-job.ts:56 (makeTuning duel baseline), :57 (census(undefined, difficulty)), :19 (ForecastRequest {id, tuning, lab}) and forecast-client.ts:26 (key = JSON.stringify([tuning, lab])). lab-ui.ts:873 'Census forecast vs Current' and the absolute-only builds duel line (~:899) verified; lab-ui.ts:1042-1043 export notice verified; forecast.ts:57-63 forecastDeltas is baseline-agnostic. Case 5's total formula matches forecast.test.ts:35. DUPLICATE: arena-progression-tuning B proposes the same pinned forecast baseline (ForecastRequest.baseline, a memoised baseline census/duel, 'vs <name>' label, the same three game files plus lab-ui.ts). This card should survive: it pins tuning AND both sides' builds (the builds page gets its first comparative read), and it leaves core forecast.ts untouched, while APT B rewrites isCurrentTuning on the census path. APT B should be voided, or narrowed to its tuningDiff changed-knobs readout layered on this baseline.
verdicts.ambition_why: Makes the Lab's iteration question ('better than five minutes ago?') answerable in one press, on both tuning and builds.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every claim stands, but four anchors cite line numbers beyond the end of their files.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Delta negation, memo reuse totals and client keying (cases 3, 5, 6) would each fail on a wrong build.
verdicts.revision: Fold in arena-progression-tuning B's changed-knobs readout as the merged survivor: add packages/core/src/arena/tuning.ts (pure tuningDiff) and a new packages/core/src/arena/tuning.test.ts to the write set and adopt APT B's acceptance cases 1-3 (tuningDiff empty / one knob with label+unit / spell override add-remove), then void APT B as the duplicate.

verdicts.title: Screen router: registry + navigation stack replacing the shell's hand-lists
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified game-shell.ts:48-66 shared per-screen fields, :53 returnScreen, the live hand-list at :198-202, the overlay list at :266, resume() at :284-292 and redraw() at :294-305 (else -> camp()). I traced the bug: training/roster are reachable from the shell (screens/training.ts:92, compose.ts:182-192). There phase comes from DEFEATED (arena-entry.ts:1071-1073), so after a defeat results() runs, the player can pause from results (results.ts:104-112), and resume() unpauses into the HUD because arena.games is undefined. results never re-fires because phase === lastPhase (:1077). saves.ts:84/99/113 returnScreen use verified. The write set is not honest for 'each screen module exports its spec': calendar() lives in screens/calendar.ts, trial() in screens/trial.ts and menu() in screens/menu.ts (menu -> saves -> back, case 3), and none of those is in the write set.
verdicts.ambition_why: Makes navigation data before D3 4.3 adds more screens, and closes a real stuck-state bug.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor holds and the headline bug reproduces by reading the code.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 1 is today's bug as a failing test; the derived-list equalities (case 4) and the throw-on-unregistered case (7) catch silent fallbacks.
verdicts.revision: Declare all screen specs in one registry table inside screens/router.ts (it imports the existing screen functions), not one spec export per screen module. calendar.ts, trial.ts and menu.ts then need no edit, and the write set stays within the files listed.
extra_files_needed: packages/game/src/screens/menu.ts (only if the per-module spec design is kept)
verdicts.build_notes: Shares game-shell.ts/chrome.ts/listen.ts with game-shell-ui B and director B (refresh change detection), and camp.ts/parley.ts with camp-season B: build this one first.

verdicts.title: Rebindable controls: one binding table drives input, remap screen and all hints
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified input.ts:48-51 (Space roll, /^Digit[1-5]$/) and :176-198 (KeyW/A/S/D, Space, ShiftLeft/Right); arena-hud.ts:260 and :441 '1-4 spells' against school-hud.ts:32-33 slotCount = 5 for Fire/Air (a real drifted hint); pause.ts:64-69 static control prose; listen.ts:52 footer and :60 KeyA/KeyD literal. Anchor drift: settings.ts is 120 lines, so ':213-232, :256-274' is really validateSettings at :52-70, which does rebuild field by field, so the additive-field and downgrade-safety claim holds. Also note input.ts:45 preventDefault is keyed to the literal 'Space'/'ArrowUp'/'ArrowDown', and a rebound key will need it too. No remap/rebind entry in tiger/backlog.md or the spark ideas.
verdicts.ambition_why: A standard, missing PC option done properly (one table for input and every hint); solid product work, not a principal's reframe.
verdicts.grounding_why: All behavioural claims hold; the settings anchors point past the end of the file.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: The default-table no-regression, conflict swap, reserved refusal, derived '1-5 spells' hint and listen rebinding are each a crisp failing-first test.
verdicts.build_notes: Build after game-shell-ui A (register 'controls' as a router spec). The builder must route input.ts's preventDefault list through the table so a rebound roll key does not scroll the page.

verdicts.title: Event-to-cue routing as data: one pure router replaces the arena hand-switch
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified arena-entry.ts:1091-1142 consumeEvents (the perfect/unlock/release/hit/stagger/roll chain interleaved with impactClock, perfectGain and the collar notice); audio-events.test.ts:16-24 hand table, :30 uncued list, :74 literal-only regex; core types.ts:87 ArenaEvent kinds (10). Arithmetic in cases 2 and 4 checks against audio.json spatial {rangeM 36, minGain 0.15}. Note: audio.json also declares maxPan 0.75, which arena-entry does not apply today. Case 2 (pan 0.5) is fine, but the router must reproduce today's unclamped pan, not 'fix' it silently.
verdicts.ambition_why: A worthwhile data seam ahead of D2 4.5, but it moves a ~30-line switch into a table rather than changing what the game can do.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor holds, and the test's blindness to template/ternary cues is real.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Exact pan/gain/cue outputs and the derived uncued list catch a wrong router; case 8's template resolution is a check the current test cannot make.
verdicts.build_notes: Shares arena-entry.ts with arena-render A/B, game-shell-ui B and smoke-browser-suite A. Game-audio-art-data B consumes this card's router.

verdicts.title: Cue sheet for the owner listening pass: a scripted bout's audio, drops explained
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified D2 doc 4.5 'An owner listening pass with a scripted bout as the fixed test' (:116), audio.json:2 label, audio-policy.ts:112-144 admit() pure, audio.ts:393-403 live-only use and the log on drop, and manifest durations exist (public/audio/manifest.json 'duration'). Defect in case 3: 'impact' has concurrency 3 in audio.json, so '8 impact sounding' is unreachable under admit(), and the case as written cannot be set up through the policy it claims to mirror. Also packages/game/scripts holds only .mjs smoke scripts; tsx-run TS tools live in packages/tools/src (root package.json).
verdicts.ambition_why: A useful operator instrument for the AU4 gate, but a text report that supports the listening pass rather than replacing it.
verdicts.grounding_why: Anchors hold, but one acceptance case contradicts the cue data it reads.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cooldown/concurrency/steal rows and byte-identical reruns are testable first, once case 3 is made reachable.
verdicts.revision: Rewrite case 3 so the effects bus is filled within each cue's concurrency (e.g. impact x3 + cast.fire x3 + hit x2 = 8 effects, then 'perfect' priority 0) and assert that the stolen row is the oldest priority-2 sound, matching admit() at audio-policy.ts:112.
verdicts.build_notes: Prefer packages/tools/src/audio-cuesheet.ts run by tsx (the house convention for TS CLIs) over packages/game/scripts/*.mts. Depends on game-audio-art-data A for silentKinds.

verdicts.title: One Director call pipeline: harness, CampNight and Parley share source resolution
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified harness.ts:55-84, camp-night.ts:60-93 (it reads the cache before the planner check; no forceLive/uncachedRaw) and parley.ts:169-223 (its own timeout/abort race) as three copies; raw cached before validation at harness.ts:74-76 and camp-night.ts:88-91, against parley.ts:211 'Cache only after validation'; camp-night.test.ts:125 misnamed; camp-night.ts:36 and :51-59 build request+key twice. Hidden hazard in the design: PlannerProvider is constructed with the base tables and a live-state getter (camp-runtime.ts:19 `new PlannerProvider(tables, () => service.session.camp)`), while CampNight runs on remainingCaps(...) and a dusk snapshot (camp-service.ts:180-186). Routing CampNight's planner path 'through PlannerProvider' would plan from different tables/state and can move planner nights (case 7 would catch it, but the stated design invites it). Parley caches the validated, repaired proposal rather than the raw reply, so 'validated' policy must cache a transform. call.ts/call.test.ts sit under new_files but not under write_set.
verdicts.ambition_why: Collapses three diverging transport chains into one with an explicit cache policy, which is where every future Director transport feature lands.
verdicts.grounding_why: The divergences are all real; the PlannerProvider shortcut rests on an unstated assumption that its tables and state are CampNight's.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Stub-driven source cases plus the W0 golden and planner-season replay give a strong outcome guard.
verdicts.revision: resolveCall's planner branch calls plan(tables, state, id, false, draws) with the caller's own tables and state (CampNight: remainingCaps + its dusk snapshot) instead of PlannerProvider.decide, so planner draws are recorded without reading PlannerProvider's base tables or live session state.
verdicts.build_notes: Build before director B; both write camp-night.ts and camp-night.test.ts, and B's progress() reads the audit rows A reshapes.

verdicts.title: Night ledger: show which tents the Director has decided before the player meets dawn
verdicts.premise_notes: Verified camp-service.ts:81-112 view() (settling + parley only), camp-night.ts:18-26 completed/audit, startNight at dusk (:176/:180-186), dawn -> finish -> CampNight.finish(graceMs) racing a timeout, camp-play.json:186 graceMs 12000, the blind dawn buttons at chrome.ts:217-231 and listen.ts:112-124, and game-shell.ts:192-195 change detection. SeasonService.view spreads super.view() (season-service.ts:12-13), so a CampService field reaches SeasonView with no hand edit, as claimed. Gap: a CampNight restored from a checkpoint is closed with undecided groups missing from completed (camp-night.ts:38-42), and after close() unfinished groups are sealed to habit. Neither state is covered, and a naive progress() would report them 'deciding' forever. night-status.ts/test sit under new_files but not under write_set.
verdicts.ambition_why: Turns a silent 12 s freeze into an informed choice and puts live Director health in the camp; real player and operator value from state that already exists.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited anchor and the view plumbing hold.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Progress counts per source and the label/subtitle mapping are crisp, but the closed and restored night states are not exercised.
verdicts.revision: Add case 8: for a closed CampNight (after close(), or restored from a checkpoint) with groups missing from completed, progress() reports pending false and those groups as 'planner' (habit), never 'deciding'.
verdicts.build_notes: After director A. Shares game-shell.ts/chrome.ts/listen.ts with game-shell-ui A and B.
